sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Omenkillers** are Enemies and optional Bosses in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Omenkillers are stoic court Perfumers who continue the grisly work of Rollo, a famed chemist of antiquity, who slaughtered accursed Omen with brutal efficiency after imbibing a physick that stripped him of emotion. They wear thick yellow aprons with front pouches and green masks with twisted horns, carved to resemble the malevolent, smirking elder spirits that torment Omen in their nightmares. Their accessories include red cloth collars, golden chainlink necklaces, and brooches with overlapping rings that likely portray the Elden Ring. The hideous severed horns crudely affixed to their paired great cleavers are trophies, gathered from their victims across the Lands Between.

Some Omenkillers joined the crusade against the hornsent, later policing rebels at the Fort of Reprimand.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
An Omenkiller found in the Village of the Albinaurics in Liurnia of the Lakes, across the bridge from the Site of Grace. This Omenkiller appears to be responsible for the slaughter of the Albinaurics on the orders of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing. This Omenkiller is accompanied by three dogs. Nepheli Loux, Warrior is available as a summon for this boss, provided she was spoken to at the entrance to the Village of the Albinaurics.

A magic user with a guided bolt-like spell such as Glintstone Pebble has a particularly efficient tactical option for this Omenkiller: the area he is in also contains two cabins. The double-jump of Torrent can easily get you onto the lower cabin, and from there another double-jump can get you onto the roof of the taller one. From there, the Omenkiller will not be able to reach you with any of his attacks. He does often get rather close to the wall of the cabin which can be difficult for you to hit, and at longer range (usually after a fire-breath when he backs up a bit) he tends to dodge attacks, but carefully timing your shots should slowly but surely allow you to kill this enemy solo at little risk.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: An Omenkiller fought alongside Miranda the Blighted Bloom at the end of the Perfumer's Grotto on the Altus Plateau.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- At least one Omenkiller worked for Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing. Another became one of Pidia's puppets, found in his storeroom at Three Sisters.
- The presence of Omenkillers among Messmer's forces in the Shadow Realm confirms the Omen and Seedbed Curse predate Queen Marika's attack on the hornsent.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Internal Name: **Slaughter**
- The Omenkiller was named **Forsaken** in .
- These enemies use the same model rigging as the Capra Demons from the first *Dark Souls* game. They have a very similar jumping slam attack. However, a Capra Demon only does one, whereas an Omenkiller would do it three times in a row. Strays harass the player during the first encounter for both enemies in their respective games.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Purchase**: Roundtable Hold

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Grants the right-hand weapon a Weapon Buff giving bonus Holy Attack Power equal to 75% of the Faith scaling of the Sacred Seal used to cast it for 90 seconds.

Also grants the weapon a 100% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death and immediately kills Skeletons after defeating them, preventing their resurrection mechanic.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 10 points of Stamina to cast.
- Despite being a Golden Order Incantation, this spell, like other spell-based weapon buffs, does not get bonus damage from its associated seal (the Golden Order Seal for this one). Additionally, said seal is actually rather bad for casting this spell as its Intelligence scaling will not be used for the weapon buff's strength.
- The moderate investment in Intelligence required for this spell is somewhat inconvenient since it does not help its scaling. The best way to cast this in limited situations is to equip the Stargazer Heirloom with an innate Intelligence of 8-12. This is possible for every Origin without an Intelligence investment, except for the Hero and the Prophet, both of which have a 7 in that Attribute.
- Like with all spell-based Weapon Buffs, it can only be cast when a weapon is held in the right hand and the casting implement in the left hand.
 - If you wish to buff two weapons at the same time, see below for similar skills.
- Outmatched by Holy Grease below 114 Incantation Scaling, by Skill: Sacred Blade below 120 Incantation Scaling, and by Golden Grease Shadow of the Erdtree below 160 Incantation Scaling.
 - Though they cast much quicker and last for a shorter duration, Drawstring Holy Grease is stronger below 147 Incantation Scaling while Drawstring Golden Grease Shadow of the Erdtree is stronger below 180 Incantation Scaling.
 - Sacred Blade has the advantage of also being usable for weapons with the otherwise unbuffable (not counting other skills) Lightning and Sacred Affinity weapons.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Protection of the Erdtree** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Erdtree Worship incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Guaranteed Drop:** Altus Plateau
- Protection of the Erdtree is obtained upon defeating a Teardrop Scarab located on a square platform upon a hill southeast of the Road of Iniquity Side Path Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Protection of the Erdtree grants a Body Buff that decreases Fire, Holy, Lightning, and Magic damage taken by 30% (10% in PvP) for 70 seconds for the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 30 FP per cast.
- Costs 50 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *ProtectionOfTheErdtree* represents the effect magnitude:
 TotalAffinityReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {AffinityDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {ProtectionOfTheErdtree}) ) 
 - For example, if affinity damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
 TotalAffinityReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.30) ) = 51.25% 
 - Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
 TotalAffinityReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as non-physical damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple non-physical damage negation sources.
- Protection of the Erdtree is a versatile defensive incantation that protects both the caster and allies from multiple damage types, making it invaluable in varied combat scenarios. Due to its accessibility early in the game, it does not require extensive stat investments, allowing many players to utilize it effectively.
- This spell is particularly useful against enemies that deal elemental damage, especially during encounters with groups or multi-phase bosses that utilize different affinities.
- While it is the weakest defensive Body Buff incantation, it strengthens all non-Physical damage negations, making it useful as a Furled Finger for not having to carry multiple defensive incantations when summoned via Summoning Pools.
- Opaline Pickled Liver

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Unlike other advanced defensive incantations, Flame, Protect Me only affects the caster. Therefore, Protection of the Erdtree is the only way to grant nearby allies protection specifically against Fire damage.
 - Protection of the Erdtree is accessible earlier than its counterparts.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The are unseen, enigmatic entities wielding immense power and influence over the world of Elden Ring, often acting indirectly to reshape the Lands Between according to their inscrutable designs. They manifest through various natural or supernatural phenomena, often tied to one or more divine elements.

sections.heading: Formless Mother
sections.markdown:
The Formless Mother, also known as the Mother of Truth, is an arcane outer god associated with Omen, hornsent, blood, and bloodflame. She craves wounds and is said to bestow power upon those born with accursed blood. The Blood Oath incantations channel her divine element, accessed by puncturing her omnipresent body with ritual spears. It is believed that the eternal blood of the Formless Mother will never dry or turn to rot.

Her current followers are Mohg, the Lord of Blood; his Mohgwyn Dynasty; and the bloodfiends, former hornsent.

sections.heading: Outer God of Death
sections.markdown:
An outer god of Death once held influence over the Lands Between. Its powers presumably included Death Blight, Spectral Light, and the Ghostflame wielded by the ancient Deathbirds and Gravebirds. This entity may also be connected to spirit-calling hexes.

The Twinbird and White-Winged Maidens are said to be the envoys of Death. After his burial at the roots of the Erdtree, Godwyn the Golden was transformed into the Prince of Death.

sections.heading: Outer God of Frenzied Flame
sections.markdown:
This theoretical outer god is representated by the maddening, yellow Flame of Frenzy; however, it is unclear whether the Frenzied Flame itself embodies this divinity or is simply a manifestation of its power. Nonetheless, its purpose is to catalyze the reunification of the One Great by destroying the Lands Between and plunging the world into chaos. It presents profound danger to all life, possessing the ability to melt away even eternal spirits. The god is associated with the Eye of Yelough and contagious yellow embers in the eyes of its followers.

The Flame of Frenzy initially entered the world through impressions left upon the grave of an ancient god by the Readerless Fingers, likely in the Finger Ruins. Later, its use was forbidden and vehemently suppressed by the Hornsent, Queen Marika, and Melina. Its blind Finger Maiden later described its envoy as a "distant light," visible only after amassing numerous Shabriri Grapes.

The Three Fingers serve as the corporeal agents of the Frenzied Flame. Its Chaos Followers—Hyetta, Midra, Nanaya, Shabriri, Vyke, and the immured Great Caravan—await the Lord of Frenzy, who will ignite the Erdtree with the yellow flame.

sections.heading: Outer God of Night
sections.markdown:
An outer god of Night is thought to be the 'greater being' behind the Nightlord in Elden Ring Nightreign. Its power is the Night's Tide that threatens Limveld. This god is identified by bones with a distinct lifelessness, which manifest in areas under its influence, such as the central castle and beyond the Spirit Shelter gate. The Iron Menial received one such Bone-Like Stone from the Nightlord in a dream, granting it to the Recluse when he awoke. Though it held the power to expunge divine essence, it could also be destroyed by it. It also held the power to alter fate, affirming a connection to the primeval current and stars.

- An eye appears in skybox for each Nightlords' arena, and is formed by the clouds above the final ring on both nights in Limveld.
- The "distinct lifelessness," "dead of night," and association with bones may imply a connection to the outer god of death, who is already connected to Night. The Black Knifeprint is composed of starlight.

sections.heading: Outer God of Rot
sections.markdown:
The outer god of Scarlet Rot whose essence was sealed away by a blind swordsman in the Lake of Rot. A great scorpion's tail, which was crafted into a dagger, is said to be a relic of this outer god. Miquella's Needle was crafted and inserted into Malenia, Blade of Miquella to ward off the affliction of the Scarlet Rot.

Its current followers include Romina, Saint of the Bud; Sage Gowry; and the Servants of Rot.

According to Gowry's understanding, the Laws of an Order of Rot would be those of "Decay" (腐敗の律) and "Rebirth" (輪廻の理).

sections.heading: List of Unconfirmed Outer Gods
sections.markdown: This section lists the entities with a very similar role to the outer gods, but are never textually referred to as such.

sections.heading: Fell God
sections.markdown: The nameless god of fire is the source of the Giants' Flame and Giants' Flame incantations; however, it interferes with the Lands Between more directly. It is an ancient, malformed deity that was depicted with curled horns and thick braids of bright red hair. It is also tied to smithing and verdigris.

sections.heading: Blood Star
sections.markdown: The blood star is a mysterious entity responsible for Briars of Punishment and Briars of Sin, two aberrant Thorn Sorceries. These sorceries require Faith to use, which implies the blood star is something that can be worshiped, and is therefore an entity. The Guilty could only see the blood star after they were blinded.

sections.heading: Serpent-God
sections.markdown: The ancient inhabitants of Mt. Gelmir made sacrifices in the name of a Serpent-God. It is likely connected to one of the god-like snakes, such as the Abyssal Serpent and God-Devouring Serpent.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The term "outer god" may also refer to gods outside of the current order, the Golden Order.
- The outer gods may be parts of the One Great that became independent when it fractured. Some language used to describe outer gods implies they were once holy, but became fractured or corrupted in the past.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- "Outer God" refers to cosmic entities in works by , alongside the "Great Old Ones." These "Other Gods" are vast, incomprehensible deities that often exist beyond human reach. The term "Outer God" was later coined by to categorize these enigmatic beings in his expansion of the .
 - The Japanese term for was similarly pulled from Japanese translations of the Cthulu Mythos.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Parrying** is a gameplay mechanic in Elden Ring.

Parrying is a specific type of Ash of War/weapon Skill action. Usually found on shields, but not exclusively.

To successfully parry an attack means to deflect an incoming blow, which then stuns the attacker and leaves them open to a counterattack. There is also a small number of reusable Tools that can deflect specific attacks, although this deflection is not strictly a "parry".

Most Enemies in the game have some number of attacks that can be deflected via parry, including many of the Bosses, but there is no visual queue or sound effect that makes it obvious whether or not an attack can be parried.

The parry mechanic can be broken down into three parts: startup, active and recovery. During the startup animation, the character will prepare to deflect an attack and is still vulnerable. Then the parry becomes active for a certain number of time, in which an incoming attack will be deflected. Afterwards follows the recovery time of the move, in which the user is vulnerable again. When hit during the startup or recovery frames of a parry, the attack will deal stamina damage similar to blocking.

Startup, active and recovery times are measured in frames, with one frame being equal to 0.01667 seconds at 60 FPS.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Preceptor Seluvis** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Seluvis is a preceptor in service of Ranni the Witch, the last princess of Caria. He resides within a rise in the Three Sisters, openly expresses disdain towards the Tarnished speaking to them with an air of superiority and hostility.

Seluvis is a collector of "puppets"—living beings transformed into thralls through the administration of a special draught brewed using Starlight Shards. The physical bodies of these puppets are stored in a hidden cellar in the Three Sisters. In the past, Seluvis was acquainted with Gideon Ofnir, however they parted ways after he turned Dolores the Sleeping Arrow into a puppet. He was also familiar with Sellen, a sorceress who owes him a favour for assisting her when she was expelled from the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Among his collection is the body of a sorceress wearing a Witch's Glintstone Crown, into which Sellen's Primal Glintstone can be inserted to provide her with a new body full of vigor.

After becoming acquainted with the Tarnished, Seluvis asks them to give a potion to Nepheli Loux. If Nepheli drinks the potion, she will fall into a deep slumber and become a puppet, with her body residing in Seluvis' basement. Alternatively, if the Tarnished shows the potion to Gideon, he will dispose of it himself and suggest that the Tarnished tell Seluvis that they gave Nepheli the potion. The potion can also be fed to the Dung Eater, resulting in him becoming a Dung Eater Puppet instead.

When the Tarnished confronts Seluvis about his collection of puppets, he offers to brew them their own puppet in exchange for Starlight Shards. If they accept, Seluvis will later task them with retrieving an Amber Starlight, with which he brews an Amber Draught intended to turn Ranni into his puppet. Ranni sees through this treachery, however, and bids the Tarnished leave, killing them if they do not.

Whether the Tarnished aids Seluvis in his betrayal or not, he can later be found dead in his tower, in the same kneeling position as his puppets.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
Pidia's questline becomes locked after giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade, regardless of any steps already completed.
1. Follow Ranni the Witch's questline and join her service in Ranni's Rise. Speak to the projections of Blaidd, Iji, and Seluvis, and then speak to Ranni once again.
1. Visit Seluvis's Rise, south of Ranni's Rise, and speak to Seluvis. Agree to his request to obtain Seluvis's Potion.
1. Perform any one of the following to proceed with Seluvis's questline:
 1. Give Nepheli Loux the potion. In order to do this, you must have defeated the Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics and Nepheli must be in the lower level of Roundtable Hold. You will obtain Nepheli Loux Puppet from Pidia, Carian Servant at the end of his questline.
 1. Give Dung Eater the potion. In order to do this, you must have obtained a Seedbed Curse, freed Dung Eater from his gaol, defeated his dark spirit in the Capital Outskirts, and made sure Dung Eater has returned to his gaol. You will be able to obtain Dung Eater Puppet from Seluvis after this.
 1. Talk to Gideon Ofnir and give him the potion.
1. Return to Seluvis and exhaust his dialogue, regardless of the option chosen in the previous step. His shop inventory will now be available.
1. Travel to the ruins north-east of Ranni's Rise and pass through the illusory floor. Go down the steps into the cellar and interact with the message saying "Seluvis' puppet. Do not touch."
1. Return to Seluvis and select the "About your chambers" dialogue option. You will now be able to buy puppets from Seluvis in return for Starlight Shards. Buy any one of these puppets to continue.
1. Speak to Seluvis again and select the "About the scheme" dialogue option.
1. Obtain the Amber Starlight from Altus Plateau. This can be found in a small grotto north-east of the Altus Highway Junction Site of Grace, north of the giant staircase that leads to the Tree Sentinel boss fight.
1. Return to Seluvis and select the "Give Amber Starlight" dialogue option to obtain the Magic Scorpion Charm.
1. Reload the area and speak to Seluvis to obtain the Amber Draught.
1. You may attempt to give the Amber Draught to Ranni. Doing so will lock Ranni's questline, and it can only be resumed by seeking Absolution at the Church of Vows. Talking to her three times after trying to give her the draught will cause her to instantly kill you.
1. Seluvis will now be dead. His Bell bearing and armour set can be looted from his body, which can also be interacted with to access the puppet shop. Pidia will also die at this stage.
1. If Ranni is not given the Amber Draught, Seluvis will die in the same way after giving her the Fingerslayer Blade.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant are both voiced by Charles Dale, and Pidia's dialogue is found nested within Seluvis' dialogue in the game's files. Along with the pose Seluvis is found in at the end of his questline, being reminiscent of the puppets in his cellar, it is presumed that Seluvis himself is a puppet of Pidia. The reveal is foreshadowed during Seluvis's introduction at Ranni's Rise when he pauses mid-sentence before stating he lives at Seluvis's Rise.

sections.markdown: The **Numen** are a faction and base template for Character Creation in Elden Ring. The Tarnished can have the lineage and appearance of a Numen.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Numen are the descendants of denizens from another world. They are said to have come to the Lands Between from the lands of the Numen. They are long lived but seldom born, and are of the same stock as Queen Marika herself. Marika came from the Shaman Village, indicating the Numen are connected to the Shamans as well. The shamans and their Grandmother were maidens with a spiritual connection to trees and flesh prized for its affinity to meld harmoniously with that of others. They were captured, tortured, chopped up, and turned into Jar Innards by the hornsent in an attempt to rebirth undesirables.

The all-women Black Knife Assassins who murdered Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives were rumored to be Numen descendants of the Eternal City with close ties to Queen Marika.

One can also be picked up along with the Hoslow's Set and Hoslow's Petal Whip where Knight Diallos dies at the end of his quest.
 - The Numen's Rune at the Divine Tower of Caelid is looted from a noble corpse that faces the Bestial Sanctum, possibly suggesting a link between the Numen, Maliketh, the Black Blade, and the Gloam-Eyed Queen.
- Numen ancestry might explain Godwyn's Deathroot, Godrick the Grafted's affinity for grafting, and Miquella's ability to water the Haligtree with his blood.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- *Numen* is a Latin term for "divinity", "divine presence", or "divine will", and "a nod of the head", referring to a deity as it were "nodding", or making its will or its presence known. It also describes a spiritual force or influence identified with a natural object, phenomenon, or place.
 - Queen Marika nods her head upward when she tugs Rune Arcs to claim godhood at the Gate of Divinity. Her head hangs downward after she shatters the Elden Ring.

- In Japanese, the are said to be descendants of people from . ** is an ancient Japanese word referring to supernatural sojourners who bring gifts of wisdom, spiritual knowledge, luck, and happiness to village communities. According to the Japanese folklorist , *marebito* come from the .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Pidia, Carian Servant** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Pidia, Carian Servant is an Elder Albinauric Sorcerer who cares for the puppets in Caria Manor, located in northwestern Liurnia of the Lakes. He can only be reached through a secret shortcut from the Three Sisters area, go down onto the tower below Seluvis's Rise. A meek and ingratiating fellow, he will attempt to gain favor with The Tarnished (Protagonist) by selling them rare items from his storeroom. He loves his puppets with all of his silver heart but at first calls them ghastly.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Carian Manor
 - If Ranni the Witch has not been given either the Fingerslayer Blade OR Seluvis' Amber Draught, the player can find Pidia on the second floor of the Manor Lower Level Site of Grace. However, he can only be reached from the building's rooftop. To gain access to him, the player must travel to the Three Sisters and follow the clifftop above Caria Manor southwest. Once there, the player can descend several platforms in order to safely reach the Manor rooftop below. When first talking with Pidia, he will offer to sell you a number of rare items from his storeroom.
1. Carian Manor
 - If Ranni the Witch has been given either the Fingerslayer Blade OR Seluvis' Amber Draught, the player will hear Pidia crying out in pain when approaching his location. Upon reaching him, the player will find Pidia lying dead, surrounded by the puppet soldiers he once maintained. The player can loot Pidia's Bell Bearing from his corpse, as well as one of two puppets depending upon certain conditions. If the player has already given Seluvis' Potion to Nepheli Loux, Pidia will drop the Nepheli Loux Puppet. If the player has not given Seluvis' Potion to Nepheli Loux, Pidia will drop Dolores the Sleeping Arrow Puppet, instead.
